V000001.name: George Vail
V000001.bio: George Vail was a Democratic U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 4th congressional district (1853–1857). Vail worked as a lawyer and judge.

V000002.name: Henry Vail
V000002.bio: Henry Vail was a Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 9th congressional district (1837–1839).

V000003.name: Richard B. Vail
V000003.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000003.bio: Richard B. Vail was a Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 2nd congressional district (1947–1949, 1951–1953). Vail worked as a businessperson, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War I.

V000004.name: William N. Vaile
V000004.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000004.bio: William N. Vaile was a Republican U.S. Representative from Colorado (1919–1927). Vaile worked as a lawyer and was a veteran of the Mexican–American War. Vaile died in office in 1927.

V000005.name: Edward K. Valentine
V000005.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000005.bio: Edward K. Valentine was a Republican U.S. Representative from Nebraska (1879–1885). Valentine worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

V000006.name: Tim Valentine
V000006.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000006.bio: Tim Valentine was a Democratic U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 2nd congressional district (1983–1995). Valentine worked as a lawyer and was a veteran of World War II.

V000007.name: William Valk
V000007.bio: William Valk was an American (Know Nothing) U.S. Representative for New York's 1st congressional district (1855–1857). Valk worked as a physician, served in the U.S. Army and Navy and was a veteran of the Civil War.

V000008.name: Clement Vallandigham
V000008.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000008.bio: Clement Vallandigham was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 3rd congressional district (1858–1863). Vallandigham worked as a lawyer and journalist.

V000009.name: Martin Van Buren
V000009.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000009.bio: Martin Van Buren was a politician from New York who served as U.S. Senator (1821–1828) and Governor of New York (1829), changing party over time (Jacksonian, then Democratic-Republican). Van Buren also served as President of the United States (1837–1841), Secretary of State (1829–1831) and Vice President (1833–1837). Van Buren worked as a lawyer and diplomat.

V000010.name: Henry Van Aernam
V000010.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000010.bio: Henry Van Aernam was a Republican U.S. Representative from New York (1865–1869, 1879–1883). Van Aernam worked as a physician, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

V000011.name: James I. Van Alen
V000011.bio: James I. Van Alen was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 8th congressional district (1807–1809). Van Alen worked as a judge.

V000012.name: John Evert Van Alen
V000012.bio: John Evert Van Alen was a Federalist U.S. Representative for New York's 7th congressional district (1793–1799). Van Alen worked as a judge and surveyor.

V000013.name: Thomas J. Van Alstyne
V000013.bio: Thomas J. Van Alstyne was a Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 16th congressional district (1883–1885). Van Alstyne worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

V000014.name: Daniel Myers Van Auken
V000014.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000014.bio: Daniel Myers Van Auken was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 11th congressional district (1867–1871). Van Auken worked as a lawyer.

V000017.name: Joseph Vance
V000017.bio: Joseph Vance was a politician from Ohio who served as U.S. Representative (1821–1835, 1843–1847) and Governor of Ohio (1836–1838), changing party over time (Democratic-Republican, then Anti-Jacksonian, then Adams, then Whig). Vance served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the War of 1812.

V000018.name: Robert Brank Vance
V000018.bio: Robert Brank Vance was a U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 12th congressional district (1823–1825).

V000020.name: Robert J. Vance
V000020.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000020.bio: Robert J. Vance was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Connecticut's 1st congressional district (1887–1889).

V000021.name: Zebulon Vance
V000021.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000021.bio: Zebulon Vance was a politician from North Carolina who served as U.S. Representative (1857–1861), Governor of North Carolina (1862–1865, 1877–1879) and U.S. Senator (1879–1894), changing party over time (American, then Ind. Republican-Democrat, then Democrat). Vance worked as a lawyer and journalist. Vance died in office in 1894.

V000022.name: Philip Van Cortlandt
V000022.bio: Philip Van Cortlandt was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative from New York (1793–1809). Van Cortlandt served in the U.S. Army.

V000023.name: Pierre Van Cortlandt Jr.
V000023.bio: Pierre Van Cortlandt Jr. was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 3rd congressional district (1811–1813). Van Cortlandt worked as a lawyer.

V000024.name: Lionel Van Deerlin
V000024.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000024.bio: Lionel Van Deerlin was a Democratic U.S. Representative from California (1963–1981). Van Deerlin worked as a journalist and educator, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War II.

V000025.name: Arthur Vandenberg
V000025.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)

V000102.name: Earl W. Vincent
V000102.photoCredit: The Iowa Legislature (des Moines, IA)., Public domain
V000102.bio: Earl W. Vincent was a Republican U.S. Representative for Iowa's 9th congressional district (1928–1929). Vincent worked as a lawyer and judge.

V000103.name: William D. Vincent
V000103.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000103.bio: William D. Vincent was a Populist U.S. Representative for Kansas's 5th congressional district (1897–1899).

V000104.name: John Vining
V000104.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000104.bio: John Vining was a politician from Delaware who served as U.S. Representative (1789–1793) and U.S. Senator (1793–1798), changing party over time (Pro-Administration, then Federalist). Vining worked as a lawyer.

V000105.name: Carl Vinson
V000105.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000105.bio: Carl Vinson was a Democratic U.S. Representative from Georgia (1913–1965). Vinson worked as a lawyer and judge.

V000106.name: Fred M. Vinson
V000106.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000106.bio: Fred M. Vinson was a Democratic U.S. Representative from Kentucky (1924–1929, 1931–1938). Vinson also served as Secretary of the Treasury (1945–1946) and Chief Justice of the United States (1946–1953). Vinson worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War I.

V000107.name: Samuel F. Vinton
V000107.photoCredit: Engraved by Carson, Columbus, Ohio, Public domain
V000107.bio: Samuel F. Vinton was a U.S. Representative from Ohio (1823–1837, 1843–1851), changing party over time (Whig, then Adams). Vinton worked as a lawyer.

V000108.name: Peter J. Visclosky
V000108.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000108.bio: Peter J. Visclosky was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Indiana's 1st congressional district (1985–2021). Visclosky worked as a lawyer.

V000109.name: Weston E. Vivian
V000109.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000109.bio: Weston E. Vivian was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Michigan's 2nd congressional district (1965–1967). Vivian worked as an educator, served in the U.S. Navy and was a veteran of World War II.

V000110.name: Edward Voigt
V000110.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000110.bio: Edward Voigt was a Republican U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 2nd congressional district (1917–1927). Voigt worked as a lawyer and judge.

V000111.name: Lester D. Volk
V000111.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000111.bio: Lester D. Volk was a Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 10th congressional district (1920–1923). Volk worked as a lawyer and served in the U.S. Army.

V000112.name: Harold Volkmer
V000112.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000112.bio: Harold Volkmer was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Missouri's 9th congressional district (1977–1997). Volkmer worked as a lawyer and served in the U.S. Army.

V000113.name: Henry Vollmer
V000113.bio: Henry Vollmer was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Iowa's 2nd congressional district (1914–1915). Vollmer worked as a lawyer.

V000114.name: Andrew Volstead
V000114.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000114.bio: Andrew Volstead was a Republican U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 7th congressional district (1903–1923). Volstead worked as a lawyer.

V000115.name: Charles Stewart Voorhees
V000115.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000115.bio: Charles Stewart Voorhees was a Democratic territorial Delegate from Washington (1885–1889). Voorhees worked as a lawyer.

V000116.name: Daniel W. Voorhees
V000116.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000116.bio: Daniel W. Voorhees was a Democratic politician from Indiana who served as U.S. Representative (1861–1866, 1869–1873) and U.S. Senator (1877–1897). Voorhees worked as a lawyer.

V000117.name: Charles H. Voorhis
V000117.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000117.bio: Charles H. Voorhis was a Republican U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 5th congressional district (1879–1881). Voorhis worked as a lawyer and judge.

V000118.name: Jerry Voorhis
V000118.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000118.bio: Jerry Voorhis was a Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 12th congressional district (1937–1947). Voorhis worked as an educator.

V000119.name: John M. Vorys
V000119.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000119.bio: John M. Vorys was a Republican U.S. Representative for Ohio's 12th congressional district (1939–1959). Vorys worked as a lawyer and educator, served in the U.S. Navy and was a veteran of World War I.

V000120.name: Roger Vose
V000120.bio: Roger Vose was a Federalist at-large U.S. Representative from New Hampshire (1813–1817). Vose worked as a lawyer and judge.

V000121.name: Albert L. Vreeland
V000121.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000121.bio: Albert L. Vreeland was a Republican U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 11th congressional district (1939–1943). Vreeland worked as a lawyer and judge and served in the U.S. Army.

V000122.name: Edward B. Vreeland
V000122.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000122.bio: Edward B. Vreeland was a Republican U.S. Representative from New York (1899–1913). Vreeland worked as a lawyer and businessperson.

V000123.name: Peter D. Vroom
V000123.bio: Peter D. Vroom was a Democratic politician from New Jersey who served as Governor of New Jersey (1829–1832, 1833–1836) and U.S. Representative (1839–1841). Vroom worked as a lawyer and diplomat.

V000124.name: Barbara Vucanovich
V000124.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000124.bio: Barbara Vucanovich was a Republican U.S. Representative for Nevada's 2nd congressional district (1983–1997).

V000125.name: Charles W. Vursell
V000125.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000125.bio: Charles W. Vursell was a Republican U.S. Representative from Illinois (1943–1959). Vursell worked as a journalist and businessperson.

V000126.name: George Voinovich
V000126.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000126.bio: George Voinovich was a Republican politician from Ohio who served as Governor of Ohio (1991–1998) and U.S. Senator (1999–2011). Voinovich also served as Mayor of Cleveland (1980–1989). Voinovich worked as a lawyer.

V000127.name: David Vitter
V000127.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000127.bio: David Vitter was a Republican politician from Louisiana who served as U.S. Representative (1999–2005) and U.S. Senator (2005–2017). Vitter worked as a lawyer and educator.

V000128.name: Chris Van Hollen
V000128.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000128.bio: Chris Van Hollen is a Democratic politician from Maryland who has served as U.S. Representative (2003–2017) and U.S. Senator (since 2017). Van Hollen worked as a lawyer.

V000129.name: David G. Valadao
V000129.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000129.bio: David G. Valadao is a Republican U.S. Representative from California (2013–2019, since 2021). Valadao worked as a farmer and businessperson.

V000130.name: Juan Vargas
V000130.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000130.bio: Juan Vargas is a Democratic U.S. Representative from California, in office since 2013. Vargas worked as a lawyer and businessperson.

V000131.name: Marc A. Veasey
V000131.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000131.bio: Marc A. Veasey is a Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 33rd congressional district, in office since 2013. Veasey worked as a journalist.

V000132.name: Filemon Vela
V000132.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000132.bio: Filemon Vela was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 34th congressional district (2013–2022). Vela worked as a lawyer.

V000133.name: Jefferson Van Drew
V000133.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000133.bio: Jefferson Van Drew is a U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 2nd congressional district, in office since 2019, changing party over time (Democrat, then Republican).

V000134.name: Beth Van Duyne
V000134.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000134.bio: Beth Van Duyne is a Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 24th congressional district, in office since 2021.

V000135.name: Derrick Van Orden
V000135.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000135.bio: Derrick Van Orden is a Republican U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 3rd congressional district, in office since 2023. Van Orden worked as a businessperson and entertainer and served in the U.S. Navy.

V000136.name: Gabe Vasquez
V000136.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000136.bio: Gabe Vasquez is a Democratic U.S. Representative for New Mexico's 2nd congressional district, in office since 2023. Vasquez worked as a journalist.

V000137.name: J.D. Vance
V000137.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000137.bio: J.D. Vance was a Republican U.S. Senator from Ohio (2023–2025). Vance also served as Vice President (since 2025). Vance worked as a lawyer and businessperson, served in the U.S. Marine Corps and was a veteran of the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.

V000138.name: Eugene Simon Vindman
V000138.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000138.bio: Eugene Simon Vindman is a Democratic U.S. Representative for Virginia's 7th congressional district, in office since 2025. Vindman worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.

V000139.name: Matt Van Epps
V000139.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
V000139.bio: Matt Van Epps is a Republican U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 7th congressional district, in office since 2025. Van Epps served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.
